tasks.subject: fix(core): teach host-local classification to see ordinary Linux filesystems (#1977)

bugReport.title: Test-runner and spawn limiters misbehave on ordinary Linux machines (tmpfs /tmp, Docker, ZFS)
bugReport.body:
On the first non-CI Linux host (WSL2, Ubuntu 26.04, where /tmp is tmpfs), 30 tests fail across three limiter test files. Watching the limiters directly: the host test-runner bound admits runs without taking a slot while reporting itself present, and the host spawn cap stops reclaiming holders from dead processes until it fills up. The same happens with a Docker container's overlay root and a ZFS root. On macOS everything works.

Expected: both host-wide limiters work on normal local Linux filesystems (tmpfs, overlay, devtmpfs, zfs), while still refusing to trust a genuinely shared network volume.

tasks.subject: fix(control-paths): an emergency stop kills and reports truthfully; the reply client keeps decision refs intact (#1976)

bugReport.title: Emergency stop says "Session terminated" but the session keeps running; tone-gate overrides are recorded as orphans
bugReport.body:
Two separate reports.

(1) Triggering an emergency stop on a running session: the route answers `killed: true`, the server log prints "killed session", and the person is told "Session terminated." The tmux session is still alive and still working afterwards.

(2) When an agent re-sends a message with `telegram-reply.sh --tone-decision-ref <ref>` after a tone-gate advisory, using a machine-prefixed ref such as `d-m_03b30f-<uuid>`, the override is recorded as an orphan outcome that matches no decision, so the gate's decision never gets graded.

Expected: an emergency stop either really ends the session or says truthfully that it did not; a valid decision ref reaches the server unchanged.

bugReport.title: Two agents in the same OpenClaw room can end up on the same Threadline thread
bugReport.body:
Intermittent e2e failure (Scenario 8, run 32674712573): `expected 'openclaw-room-a-mt6h30po' not to be 'openclaw-room-a-mt6h30po'`. Two different agents resolving a thread in the same room at nearly the same moment received the identical thread id, and their conversations were then mapped onto one thread. tasks.subject: fix(sessions): a session that exits on its own now leaves a trace (reason + reap-log row + last pane tail) (#1963)

bugReport.title: A session that exits on its own leaves no reason, no reap-log row and no clue why
bugReport.body:
On 2026-08-22 every interactive Codex session died about 18 seconds after spawn. Each one was recorded only as `status: completed` with no ended reason, nothing appeared in `GET /sessions/reap-log`, and nothing in the logs said what had been on screen. Sessions that are killed by the reaper, an operator or terminateSession all get a reason and a reap-log row; a session whose process ends by itself gets neither. The cause had to be found by hand-spawning a session and watching the pane.

Expected: a session that exits by itself is recorded with a reason (and whether it died during startup), a reap-log entry, and enough of the last screen output to debug it, without leaking credentials.

bugReport.title: Cross-machine "Set up" sign-in returns a bare 408 while the sign-in is still in progress
bugReport.body:
Tapping "Set up" on the Subscriptions grid for an account held on another machine: any sign-in that takes longer than about 30 seconds returns HTTP 408 to the dashboard, while the server keeps working on it and later reaches a real outcome (login did not start / cannot resolve email / reused) that the operator never sees. Submit-code is the worst case: the verification code is single-use, so after a 408 the operator cannot tell whether their one attempt was spent.

bugReport.title: A re-delivered inbound message looks identical to a fresh instruction
bugReport.body:
When Instar's no-loss recovery re-injects an inbound Telegram message that was claimed but never replied to, the session receives exactly the same text as the original delivery. Verified on 2026-08-20: the two injected payload files for nonce dAdM7ghJNCcFdO4I (09:45:01 and 10:10:02) have the same md5. bugReport.title: `telegram-reply.sh` prints "Sent" for messages the server suppressed as duplicates
bugReport.body:
When an agent sends the same text to the same topic twice within the duplicate window, the user receives only the first copy (expected), but for the second send `telegram-reply.sh` prints "Sent N chars" and exits 0. The agent believes the reply went out and moves on; there is no error, no retry and no log line. The server's response body for that request says the send was suppressed. Deployed agents keep the old script after updating.

Expected: the relay script reports a suppressed duplicate as not sent (non-zero exit), never reports a real send as suppressed, and existing agents receive the corrected script on update.

tasks.source: real past fix (instar main)
tasks.subject: fix(identity): require evidence for verified topic operators (#1918)

bugReport.title: Any caller can create a "verified" topic operator through the manual API
bugReport.body:
`POST /topic-operator` with any non-blank `uid` in its body stores a record with the same `authenticated-inbound` provenance as an operator bound from a real authorized Telegram message. Reading the store afterwards, there is no way to tell the manually asserted uid from a genuinely authenticated one, and downstream readers (session-context injection, outbound review, replication to other machines) treat it as the verified operator. Older records carry no evidence at all and are treated the same way.

Expected: only an operator established from an authenticated inbound message counts as verified; manual assertions and evidence-less records stay inspectable but grant no authority, and an authorized message re-establishes a legacy topic.

tasks.subject: fix(follow-me): keep the account's provider/framework when it lives on a peer (#1912)

bugReport.title: Following a Codex account to another machine runs the Claude sign-in flow and loops
bugReport.body:
Starting a cross-machine follow-me for a Codex account that is held only on a peer machine: the receiving machine treats it as an Anthropic / Claude Code account, starts the Claude url-code-paste sign-in, and writes into a `~/.claude-followme-*` home that Codex never reads. The login never finishes and the follow-me is re-driven on a cadence indefinitely. Verified live: the laptop recorded codex-sagemindai as anthropic/claude-code under ~/.claude-followme-codex-sagemindai while the Mini holds it as openai/codex-cli; the server log loops started-login → HELD (missing-completed-email).

Expected: a follow-me keeps the account's real provider and framework, uses a home that framework reads, and stops rather than looping when machines disagree about what kind of account it is.

tasks.subject: fix(lint): url-log guard resolves a credentialed URL split across a concatenation (#1893)

bugReport.title: URL-logging lint misses a credentialed URL split across a string concatenation
bugReport.body:
The lint that forbids logging a URL with embedded credentials (added after `instar join` logged a clone URL carrying a live GitHub token on 2026-05-27) flags `"https://user:tok@github.com/x.git"` but does not flag `"https://user:" + "tok@github.com/x.git"`. Both build the same string and leak the same token. Splitting a long literal like this is ordinary tidying a formatter may do, so the lint can be disarmed by accident.

Expected: a credentialed URL built from adjacent string literals is flagged the same as a single literal, without new false positives on code that joins a literal with a variable.
